subject.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync

question: Should externally provisioned sandbox skills be represented by a backend capability that returns readable container paths, or should OpenClaw accept `agents.*.sandbox.docker.skipSkillsSync` as a permanent public config contract?
rationale: The configuration surface bar is high, and skipping materialization is safe only when another owner guarantees both provisioning and canonical prompt-readable paths; implementation alone cannot choose that permanent ownership boundary.

options.title: Use a backend capability
options.body: Have capable sandbox backends declare externally provisioned skills and their readable container paths, avoiding a broad operator knob with unverifiable path assumptions.

options.title: Keep the config option
options.body: Accept the opt-in setting only after defining a canonical preinstalled path contract, preserving every prompt surface, adding upgrade documentation, and providing live repeated-setup proof.

options.title: Decline the optimization
options.body: Close the PR and linked request if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to support externally managed sandbox skill provisioning.

recommendation.title: Use a backend capability
recommendation.body: Have capable sandbox backends declare externally provisioned skills and their readable container paths, avoiding a broad operator knob with unverifiable path assumptions.

likelyOwner.reason: The sandbox backend architecture and repository leadership history make steipete the strongest available owner for this config-versus-capability decision.
